question.problem:
Rationalize the denominator of the following expression:
$\sqrt{\frac{11}{pq}}\,=\,$ {{field-1}}
$pq$

current_example.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{3}{8a}} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{8a}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to remove the radical $\sqrt{8a}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{8a}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{8a}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{8a}}{\sqrt{8a}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{24a}}{(\sqrt{8a})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{4\cdot 6a}}{8a} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6a}}{8a} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{6a}}{4a}\end{aligned}
$$
